environment.renderer: ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (0x00002C05) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)
environment.mode: System Chrome, headless, Windows, offline local fixtures

presentation.method: Unique Display::FrameDisplayed timestamps during 2 s of pointer movement driven by real rAF over a stationary 1000-row table, or a native 4800 CSS px scroll gesture. Interleaved A/B. Medians of per-trial FPS and frame-interval percentiles. Raw offsets are microseconds from the trial start mark.

detailFirstPresentation.method: Trusted click reveals a preloaded details page. Element Timing reports presentation of its title and of a marker inserted when all native glass maps have decoded. Fresh context and map cache for each trial; round zero excluded.
detailFirstPresentation.caveat: Image decoded before trusted click. Title is first presented text. Ready marker presents after all requested maps have decoded and is an upper bound for material readiness; includes marker/compositor scheduling.

pointerMaterial.region: all physical pixels strictly inside the scrollport bounds, with foreground rows and text
pointerMaterial.method: PointerEvent alternates between two subpixel coordinates within the same 0.1 CSS pixel light pose. Table scrollTop is unchanged. Same browser compares full, active and full-again frames. After input stops, compare the restored frame with a forced full frame. Raw differences include repeated-full variation.

validation.liveCanvas: 125% DPR deep in stationary table, red/blue while pointer moving and again after pause. Low/reduced/fixed/none escape paths exercised.
validation.workerCoverage: Same key requested twice, second slot for distinct work, withdrawn queued request, stale result after resize, detach while running, cached hit, idle pool termination and restart, 2 logical cores use 1 slot, synchronous fallback on failed startup or worker error, decoded RGBA equality for asymmetric radii.

staticSwitchBoundary.comparison: The unchanged native filter produced two distinct whole-page hashes at a single stationary pose. The regression requires an exact match against one of the reference captures for that same pose.
